To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

exposure to endogenous LPS (eLPS), during sensitization to Blomina tropicalis allergens, results in a shift in the TH2 immune response towards a TH17-mediated airway neutrophili inflammation, which is dependent on TLR4 and on TLR2 signaling.
exposure to endotoxic lipopolysacchaides during sensitization to Blomis tropicalis allergens induces a TH17 mediated airway neutrophila that is dependent on TLR4 and to a lesser extend on TLR2.

exposure to endogenous LPS (eLPS), but not to ultrapurified LPS (up LPS), during sensitization to the house dust mites allergens, Blomia tropical is, results in the induction of a neutrophilic airway inflammation that is dependent on TLR4 and IL-17RA.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the role of endotoxin in the regulation of the immune response to inhaled allergens.
the role of endotoxin and TLR signaling during the development of allergic airway inflammation.
the role of TLRs in the pathogenesis of allergic airway inflammation.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
eLPS exposure in the sensitization phase of the Bt model of asthma induces a TH2-to-TH17 switch that results in an airway neutrophili
the exposure to eLPs during sensitization with Bt allergen induces a TH17-mediated neutrophilic airway inflammation.
eLPS exposure to Bt allergen during sensitization induces a TH17-mediated airway neutrophiliac inflammation that is dependent on TLR4 and on TLR2.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
exposure to eLP during allergen sensitization can shift TH2 immunity towards a TH17-mediated airway neutrophili

exposure to endotoxic lipopolysacchaide (eLps) during sensitization to allergens derived from the house mite Blomis tropicalis (B. tropicalis) results in the induction of airway neutrophillar inflammation associated with an increase in the frequency of lung Th17 cells.
TLR4 activation during sensitization to allergens induces a TH2 immune response while TLR2 activation induces TH17 immune response that is independent of MyD88 and CD14.
The main takeaway from our work is that
exposure to bacterial products or TLR ligands during sensitization with allergens may result in the induction of a neutrophilic lung inflammation.
TLR4 and to a lesser extent TLR2 signaling is involved in airway neutrophic inflammation.
TLR agonists can be used to treat allergic asthma but the choice of TLR agonists should be carefully made.
